views.name: ball_event_with_players
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker_batting_position,
  b.striker,
  striker_player.player_name AS striker_player_name,
  b.non_striker,
  non_striker_player.player_name AS non_striker_player_name,
  b.bowler,
  bowler_player.player_name AS bowler_player_name,
  m.match_date,
  m.season_id,
  m.venue,
  m.team_1,
  m.team_2,
  m.toss_winner,
  m.toss_decision,
  m.match_winner
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN player striker_player ON b.striker = striker_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN player non_striker_player ON b.non_striker = non_striker_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN player bowler_player ON b.bowler = bowler_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN match m ON b.match_id = m.match_id

params.description: Row-level ball-by-ball view enriched with player and match attributes for each delivery (grain: match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id).

params.metric: This view exposes no aggregated measures at its own grain — all columns are sourced attributes. If you create derived metrics, define them explicitly after joining (examples): | deliveries_count = COUNT(*) over desired grouping (explicit aggregation; not computed in view) | unique_bowlers_count = COUNT(DISTINCT bowler) over grouping (explicit aggregation) | Note: do not assume precomputed aggregates exist in this view; it is a 1:1 row per ball fact enrichment.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like tables or one-row-per-entity views on their natural keys — safe because they do not multiply this view's rows. | Safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): | - join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match (no duplication of ball rows). | - join to player_match_roster on (match_id, player_id) but only when roster is one-row-per-player-per-match (ensure its grain is player+match); if roster is one-row-per-player-per-match it is safe for player-level enrichment. | Do NOT join without care (these will multiply rows/measures unless you aggregate first): | - do NOT join directly to one-to-many ball-level fact views such as extras_per_ball_with_type, batsman_runs_per_ball, or wickets_with_kind_and_player without ensuring you preserve or re-aggregate cardinality — these are also ball-grain and may be one-to-many per ball (e.g., multiple extra types, multiple wicket events) and will duplicate this view's row-level semantics. | - do NOT join to player_match_roster or other roster views if they are one-to-many (e.g., multiple role rows per player per match) without reducing to one row per (match_id, player_id). | Recommended safe composition patterns: | - To aggregate measures per-match/over/innings: aggregate this view (GROUP BY match_id[, innings_no[, over_id]]) then join to other aggregated datasets. | - To add ball-level metrics provided by sibling ball-grain views (batsman_runs_per_ball, extras_per_ball_with_type, wickets_with_kind_and_player): join on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) only when those sibling views are known to be strictly one-row-per-ball or when you plan to re-aggregate after join. If the sibling view is one-row-per-ball, the join is 1:1 and safe; if it is one-to-many, aggregate sibling first (e.g., SUM/ranking) to avoid multiplication. | - To enrich player attributes for a particular role (striker/non_striker/bowler): this view already left-joins player names by player_id. If you need additional player-level attributes from player or player-match tables, join on player_id for the specific role and ensure the player-side is one-row-per-player (or pre-aggregated to one row per player). | Practical keys to use for joins: | - Ball-level joins: (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) — use only with other views/tables that are one-row-per-ball or aggregated to ball-level. | - Match-level joins: match_id — use with one-row-per-match tables/views. | - Player-level joins: player_id (and match_id if using player-match scoped data) — ensure the right grain (player vs player+match).

views.name: batsman_runs_per_ball
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  p.player_name AS striker_player_name,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM batsman_scored bs
JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN player p ON b.striker = p.player_id

params.description: Per-ball batsman scoring: one row per ball indicating the striker and runs scored by that batsman on that ball.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the batsman and runs scored for each individual legal delivery (ball) in a match/innings/over. | Compute further aggregations by composing per-ball runs into per-over, per-innings or per-player metrics (after appropriate aggregation). | Join ball-level player metadata (e.g., striker name) to ball-level events or stats.
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived from ball_by_ball.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from ball_by_ball.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings — derived from ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over — derived from ball_by_ball.ball_id | striker: player_id of the batsman on strike for that ball — derived from ball_by_ball.striker | striker_player_name: player_name corresponding to striker — derived from player.player_name (LEFT JOIN on player.player_id) | runs_scored: runs scored by the batsman on that ball — derived from batsman_scored.runs_scored
params.grounded_columns: batsman_scored.match_id | batsman_scored.innings_no | batsman_scored.over_id | batsman_scored.ball_id | batsman_scored.runs_scored | ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.striker | player.player_id | player.player_name
params.metric: runs_scored = batsman_scored.runs_scored (atomic, per-row metric; NOT an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional/look-up views/tables one-to-one with this view's grain without aggregating — safe examples: |  - Join to player_match_roster on (striker = player_id AND match_id) — safe because player_match_roster is expected to be at most one row per player per match, so it will not duplicate runs_scored. |  - Join to player (or any player-level one-row-per-player table) on (striker = player_id) — safe because player is one-row-per-player and does not duplicate ball-level measures. |  - Join to match_summary_basic on (match_id) — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match and will not multiply ball rows. |  | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views that expand rows per ball (without re-aggregation) because they will multiply runs_scored and other per-ball measures. Examples to avoid or to use only after aggregation: |  - Do NOT join directly to extras_per_ball_with_type (if that view can contain multiple extra rows per ball) unless you first aggregate extras to ball-level; otherwise runs_scored may be duplicated. |  - Do NOT join directly to ball_event_with_players if that view contains multiple event rows per ball (e.g., multiple events recorded for the same ball) without ensuring event-level deduplication or aggregation to the same grain (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id). |  - Do NOT join directly to wickets_with_kind_and_player without confirming it is at most one row per ball; if wickets_with_kind_and_player can contain multiple rows per ball (e.g., multiple wicket records), aggregate or deduplicate to ball-level first. |  | Guidance for composing aggregations: |  - To compute per-player or per-match aggregates from this view, first aggregate runs_scored at the desired grouping (e.g., SUM(runs_scored) GROUP BY match_id, striker) before joining to any one-to-many detail tables. |  - When composing into higher-level aggregates (over-level, innings-level), group by the target grain (for example, GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id to get runs per over) so that further joins to one-to-many tables do not multiply measures. |  | Reasoning about join-safe cardinality: this view has deterministic one-row-per base ball identified by the grain (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) because it selects rows from batsman_scored joined to ball_by_ball on the same ball keys. As long as you join other datasets that are one-row-per-(match/ball) or one-row-per-player (when joining on striker) the per-ball atomic measure runs_scored will remain unduplicated. Any join that can introduce multiple rows for the same ball MUST be preceded by aggregation or de-duplication to the ball-level grain.

views.description: Ball-level pairing of batsman runs with ball event (to know which batsman scored on which ball). Useful for aggregations of batsman runs, strike-rate, and per-innings scoring. | Use for: Total runs by a batsman in a match/season/career; Balls where a batsman scored X runs; Strike-rate and scoring breakdown per batsman

views.name: wickets_with_kind_and_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  p.player_name AS player_out_name,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken w
LEFT JOIN player p ON w.player_out = p.player_id

params.description: Provides wicket events per ball with the dismissed player id, their name, and dismissal kind — one row per wicket-taking ball (grained by match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id).
params.when_to_use: List all wickets in a match/innings/over/ball with player identity and dismissal kind | Join wicket-level details into broader ball-level analyses without duplicating wicket attributes | Compose player-level wicket aggregations by aggregating this view (e.g., count wickets per player per match) | Enrich ball-level event streams with the dismissed batter's name and dismissal kind
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived from wicket_taken.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from wicket_taken.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings — derived from wicket_taken.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over — derived from wicket_taken.ball_id | player_out: player_id of the dismissed player — derived from wicket_taken.player_out | player_out_name: player_name of the dismissed player — derived from player.player_name (via LEFT JOIN on wicket_taken.player_out = player.player_id) | kind_out: textual code/type describing dismissal kind (e.g., 'bowled', 'caught') — derived from wicket_taken.kind_out
params.grounded_columns: wicket_taken.match_id | wicket_taken.innings_no | wicket_taken.over_id | wicket_taken.ball_id | wicket_taken.player_out | wicket_taken.kind_out | player.player_id | player.player_name
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are computed in this view; all columns are raw/passthrough from base tables. | If used as source for metrics: wicket_count = COUNT(*) when grouping by desired keys (e.g., player_out, match_id)
params.composition: Safe to join (one-to-one or many-to-one from this view's perspective): join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match, so it will not duplicate wicket rows. | Safe to join: join to player_match_roster on (match_id, player_id = player_out) — safe when player_match_roster is one-row-per-player-per-match (it enriches wicket rows without duplicating wicket measures). | Unsafe to join without re-aggregation: do NOT directly join to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, extras_per_ball_with_type, or any other ball-level one-to-many view/table on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) unless you intend to expand wicket rows — these are one-to-many relative to a single wicket row (for example, a ball may have multiple related events or extras) and will multiply counts if you treat wicket rows as atomic measures. | Unsafe to join without aggregation: do NOT join to wickets_agg_per_player_match or batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match on player/match keys expecting no duplication — those are aggregated summaries; if joined you should join on matching grain and be explicit whether you want per-wicket detail combined with per-player aggregates (prefer joining aggregated view on player+match keys where aggregated rows are one-per-player-per-match). | Guidance for building aggregations on top: when aggregating this view (e.g., COUNT(*) AS wickets_per_player_per_match GROUP BY match_id, player_out), you can safely join other one-row-per-player-per-match dimensions (player_match_roster) or one-row-per-match dimensions (match_summary_basic) afterwards without changing the aggregate semantics. If you need to join ball-level one-to-many detail to compute derived metrics, first aggregate that detail to the same grain as this view (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) or to the target aggregation grain to avoid row multiplication.

views.description: One row per wicket event including dismissed player name and basic match context. Use for per-player dismissal counts, types of dismissals, and timeline of wickets in an innings. | Use for: Count dismissals by player or by kind; Sequence of wickets in an innings or match; Which players were out and how in a match

views.name: extras_per_ball_with_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.match_id,
  e.innings_no,
  e.over_id,
  e.ball_id,
  e.extra_type,
  e.extra_runs
FROM extra_runs e

params.description: Provides one row per ball that had extra runs, listing the match, innings, over, ball identifiers, the extra type and the number of extra runs.
params.when_to_use: List or filter individual deliveries that contained extras (e.g., find all wides, no-balls, byes, leg-byes). | Compute ball-level statistics involving extras (e.g., join with ball-level events to show players involved on balls with extras). | Compose aggregated extra-run summaries by grouping these ball-level extra rows (e.g., total extra runs per match/innings/type). | Filter deliveries with extras before joining to other per-ball views (e.g., to limit further analysis to only extra deliveries).
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier; derived from base column extra_runs.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match; derived from base column extra_runs.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings; derived from base column extra_runs.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over; derived from base column extra_runs.ball_id | extra_type: categorical type of the extra (e.g., wide, noball, bye, legbye); derived from base column extra_runs.extra_type | extra_runs: number of runs awarded as extras on this ball; derived from base column extra_runs.extra_runs
params.grounded_columns: extra_runs.match_id | extra_runs.innings_no | extra_runs.over_id | extra_runs.ball_id | extra_runs.extra_type | extra_runs.extra_runs
params.metric: extra_runs = extra_runs.extra_runs  -- atomic numeric value per row (ball-level); not an aggregate in this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match, so it will not duplicate per-ball rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_roster on (match_id) and optionally player_id if filtering by player to add player-level metadata — safe only when you constrain roster to one row per player-match; joining roster without player filter may expand roster per match (one-to-many) and thus multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ball_event_with_players on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) — safe because ball_event_with_players is a per-ball normalized/joined view (one row per ball event) so it will align 1:1 with this view's ball grain and not duplicate extra_runs. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many aggregations (e.g., batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match, wickets_agg_per_player_match) without re-aggregation or proper grouping first — those are aggregated at player-match grain and can create many-to-one relationships that duplicate this view's ball rows unless you aggregate the joined side back to the ball or to the same grain. | DO NOT join to raw event tables or views that are one-to-many at the ball grain (for example a hypothetical ball_events_with_multiple_actions per ball) unless you first aggregate those events to the ball-level, because joining a one-to-many child to this per-ball view will multiply extra_runs occurrences. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total extras per match or per innings), aggregate extra_runs after selecting/joining: SELECT match_id, SUM(extra_runs) FROM extras_per_ball_with_type GROUP BY match_id — avoid summing after joining to tables that expand rows without re-aggregation. | If you need player-level attribution (e.g., which bowler conceded an extra), join ball_event_with_players (1:1 at ball grain) first to attach the player_id, then aggregate by player_id so measures remain correct and not duplicated.

views.description: One row per ball extra runs event joined with ball identity and match/innings. Use to analyze extras by type, totals conceded by innings, or to attach extras to balls for total-run calculations. | Use for: Aggregate extras by type per match/innings/season; Compute total extras conceded by a team in an innings

views.name: player_match_roster
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  pm.role,
  pm.team_id
FROM player_match pm
LEFT JOIN player p ON pm.player_id = p.player_id

params.description: Lists roster membership of players in each match (one row per match_id, player_id) with player name, role, and team assignment.
params.when_to_use: Get the list of players who participated in a specific match (or set of matches) and their team/role. | Join player-level match metrics (runs, wickets, events) to match+player context without duplicating match/player rows. | Build per-player-per-match aggregates by joining to ball-level or event-level data (but ensuring proper aggregation to avoid duplication). | Filter or attribute match-level events to the players that were on the roster for that match.
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived directly from player_match.match_id | player_id: player identifier — derived directly from player_match.player_id | player_name: human-readable player name — derived from player.player_name (LEFT JOINed to player_match.player_id) | role: player role in that match (as stored) — derived directly from player_match.role | team_id: team identifier the player belonged to in that match — derived directly from player_match.team_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is normalized per match (one-row-per-match), so joining match_summary_basic to player_match_roster will not duplicate the roster rows; it simply enriches each match/player row with match-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match on (match_id, player_id) — safe because batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match is an aggregate at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). Measures in that view can be joined directly without re-aggregation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to wickets_agg_per_player_match on (match_id, player_id) — safe because that view is an aggregate at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_rank_top_scoring on (match_id, player_id) — safe when that view is ranked/aggregated at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). | DO NOT join directly to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, wickets_with_kind_and_player, or extras_per_ball_with_type without aggregating the ball/event-level table to match_id+player_id first — those sibling views are one-to-many (multiple events/balls per player per match), and joining them directly will multiply the roster rows and duplicate any measures from the roster-side. | If you need event/ball-level detail with roster columns present, either: (a) start from the ball/event-level view and LEFT JOIN player (or player_match) to bring in roster info, or (b) aggregate the ball/event-level view to (match_id, player_id) (e.g., SUM(runs) AS runs) before joining to this roster view to preserve one-row-per-(match_id,player_id) cardinality. | When joining to player_total_runs_season_window (a windowed metric), verify its grain. If that view is computed per player across a season window (one-row-per-player or per player+season), join on player_id only; doing so will replicate roster rows across seasons or windows if the window view has multiple rows per player — re-aggregate or filter as needed to avoid unintended duplication.

views.description: Normalized roster of players in each match with their role and team. Useful to filter players by role (Captain, Keeper) or to join match-level stats back to the player roster. | Use for: Who played in a given match and what was their role; List captains or keepers across matches; Join player-level aggregates back to the roster for match-level reporting

views.name: match_summary_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  match_date,
  season_id,
  venue,
  toss_winner,
  toss_decision,
  win_type,
  win_margin,
  outcome_type,
  match_winner,
  man_of_the_match
FROM match

params.description: A one-row-per-match summary giving basic match-level attributes (teams, date, season, venue, toss, result, margin, man-of-the-match).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve match-level metadata for reporting or joining into higher-level analyses (e.g., schedule lists, match timelines). | Serve as a dimension/source when composing match-level aggregates (e.g., counts of matches by season, venue, toss_decision, or match_winner). | Join with per-player or per-ball derived datasets to add match context (match_date, season_id, teams) while preserving match-level granularity if joins are cardinality-safe.
params.output_schema: match_id: unique identifier for the match — derived from match.match_id | team_1: first team participating in the match — derived from match.team_1 | team_2: second team participating in the match — derived from match.team_2 | match_date: date (or timestamp) the match was played — derived from match.match_date | season_id: identifier of the season the match belongs to — derived from match.season_id | venue: venue/location name or id for the match — derived from match.venue | toss_winner: team that won the pre-match toss — derived from match.toss_winner | toss_decision: the toss decision (e.g., 'bat'/'bowl') — derived from match.toss_decision | win_type: how the match was decided (e.g., 'runs', 'wickets', 'tie') — derived from match.win_type | win_margin: numeric margin of victory (runs or wickets as appropriate) — derived from match.win_margin | outcome_type: high-level outcome classification (e.g., 'normal', 'abandoned') — derived from match.outcome_type | match_winner: team that won the match (NULL if no winner) — derived from match.match_winner | man_of_the_match: player id or name awarded man-of-the-match (NULL if none) — derived from match.man_of_the_match
params.grounded_columns: match.match_id | match.team_1 | match.team_2 | match.match_date | match.season_id | match.venue | match.toss_winner | match.toss_decision | match.win_type | match.win_margin | match.outcome_type | match.match_winner | match.man_of_the_match
params.metric: No derived aggregations in this view; all outputs are direct base columns. Example forms (for planner clarity): | match_count = COUNT(match.match_id) WHEN aggregated at higher level (this view is one row per match so COUNT over match_id yields number of matches) | distinct_matches_by_season(season_id) = COUNT(DISTINCT match.match_id) — can be computed when grouping by season_id from this view

views.name: batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.striker AS player_id,
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_scored_in_match_innings
FROM batsman_scored bs
JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.striker,
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no

views.name: player_total_runs_season_window
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.player_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.season_id,
  SUM(r.runs_scored_in_match_innings) OVER (PARTITION BY r.player_id ORDER BY m.match_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_runs_by_date
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.striker AS player_id,
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_scored_in_match_innings
  FROM batsman_scored bs
  JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id, b.innings_no
) r
JOIN match m ON r.match_id = m.match_id

views.name: ball_events_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.bowler,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs
FROM ball_event_with_players AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball AS br
  ON br.match_id = b.match_id
  AND br.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND br.over_id = b.over_id
  AND br.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extras_per_ball_with_type AS e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
views.description: One row per ball delivery with canonicalized identifiers and nullable-safe numeric values for runs and extras. Normalizes ball_by_ball, batsman_scored and extra_runs into a single per-ball event with innings, match, over, ball, striker and bowler info and explicit runs fields (batsman_runs and extra_runs).

views.name: over_runs_by_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.bowler,
  SUM(
    COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)
  ) AS runs_in_over
FROM
  ball_events_canonical b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
  ON b.match_id = br.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = br.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = br.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = br.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  extras_per_ball_with_type e
  ON b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.bowler
views.description: Aggregated runs conceded for each over in a match (grouped by match_id, innings_no, over_id) and the bowler who bowled that over. Sums batsman_runs + extra_runs across all balls in the over. Includes bowler id and over-level run total so consumers can filter to match-level maxima or rank overs.

views.name: delivery_runs_and_extras
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  COALESCE(b.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs
FROM batsman_runs_per_ball b
LEFT JOIN extras_per_ball_with_type e
  ON b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id

-- include deliveries that have extras but no batsman runs row
SELECT

  e.over_id,

  e.innings_no,
  0 AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs

LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball b
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id

views.name: bowler_aggregate_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bbow.bowler AS bowler_player_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(ex.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs_conceded,
  COUNT(wt.player_out) AS total_wickets_taken
FROM ball_event_with_players AS bbow
LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball AS br
  ON bbow.match_id = br.match_id
  AND bbow.innings_no = br.innings_no
  AND bbow.over_id = br.over_id
  AND bbow.ball_id = br.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extras_per_ball_with_type AS ex
  ON bbow.match_id = ex.match_id
  AND bbow.innings_no = ex.innings_no
  AND bbow.over_id = ex.over_id
  AND bbow.ball_id = ex.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wickets_with_kind_and_player AS wt
  ON bbow.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND bbow.innings_no = wt.innings_no
  AND bbow.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND bbow.ball_id = wt.ball_id
  AND wt.player_out IS NOT NULL
  AND wt.player_out != bbow.bowler -- ensure wicket credited to bowler (will still count catches etc. separately if recorded)
GROUP BY bbow.bowler
views.description: Aggregated bowling metrics per bowler: total_runs_conceded (sum of batsman runs + extras over deliveries they bowled) and total_wickets_taken (count of wickets credited to them). Exposes raw aggregates and leaves filtering (min wickets, ordering) to the query.

validated_on: Retrieve the names of players who scored no less than 100 runs in a match while playing for the team that lost that match.

Can you help me find the top 5 countries whose players have the highest average of their individual average runs per match across all seasons? Specifically, for each player, calculate their average runs per match over all matches they played, then compute the average of these player averages for each country, and include these country batting averages in the result.

views.name: striker_match_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  br.match_id AS match_id,
  br.striker AS striker,
  SUM(br.runs_scored) AS total_runs,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_faced
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
GROUP BY
  br.match_id,
  br.striker
views.description: Aggregate total runs for each striker within a match (grouped by match_id and striker/player_id). Sums only existing batsman_scored.runs_scored rows; does not add extras or wickets. Exposes the per-striker-per-match total that can be filtered (e.g., > 50) or averaged.

views.name: player_basic_17
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player.player_id AS player_id,
  player.player_name AS player_name,
  player.country_name AS country_name,
  player.batting_hand AS batting_hand,
  player.bowling_skill AS bowling_skill,
  player.dob AS dob
FROM player
views.description: Canonical player dimension with stable identifiers and common attributes useful for joins and filters (name, country, batting hand, bowling skill, dob).
counter_examples: For each player, list their ID, name, their most frequent role across all matches, batting hand, bowling skill, total runs scored, total matches played, total times they were dismissed, batting average (total runs divided by total dismissals), highest score in a single match, the number of matches in which they scored at least 30 runs, at least 50 runs, and at least 100 runs, total balls faced in their career, strike rate (total runs divided by total balls faced, multiplied by 100), total wickets taken, economy rate (average runs conceded per over), and their best bowling performance in a single match (most wickets taken in a match, formatted as "wickets taken-runs given", where the best performance is the one with the most wickets, and if tied, the fewest runs conceded). Ignore the extra runs data.

views.name: player_match_assignments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  match_id,
  team_id,
  role
FROM player_match_roster
views.description: Which team a player represented in a specific match (one row per player_id, match_id assignment).

views.name: match_season_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_id,
  m.season_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.team_1,
  m.team_2,
  m.venue
FROM match AS m
views.description: Subset of matches with season and basic match identifiers and teams; useful to restrict analytics to one season or to join match metadata like season_id and date.

views.name: ball_by_ball_striker_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bebp.match_id,
  bebp.over_id,
  bebp.ball_id,
  bebp.innings_no,
  bebp.striker,
  bebp.team_batting,
  bebp.team_bowling,
  bebp.bowler,
  bebp.striker_batting_position
FROM ball_event_with_players AS bebp
grain: match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no  -- one row per delivery
views.description: Ball-by-ball deliveries with the striker (batter) and identifiers needed to attribute batsman scoring events to a player and match; facilitates joining to runs, extras, wickets and counting batting appearances.

views.name: batsman_ball_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker AS "player_id  -- striker/player who faced the ball",
  bs.runs_scored AS "runs_scored  -- runs from batsman_scored for that delivery"
FROM ball_by_ball b
JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
output_columns: player_id  -- striker/player who faced the ball
runs_scored  -- runs from batsman_scored for that delivery
grain: match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no  -- one row per delivery where a batsman scoring record exists
views.description: Attribution of runs scored on a delivery to the batting player (striker) by joining ball_by_ball to batsman_scored; exposes raw runs per delivery per player for aggregation.

views.name: player_basic_22
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player.player_id AS player_id,
  player.player_name AS player_name,
  player.country_name AS country_name,
  player.dob AS dob,
  player.batting_hand AS batting_hand,
  player.bowling_skill AS bowling_skill
FROM player
WHERE player.country_name IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per player with canonical identity and demographic attributes (cleaned/canonicalized). Keep country and player identifiers for joins and grouping.

views.name: player_match_level_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.runs_scored AS total_runs, 
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.match_id) AS matches_played,
  b.striker AS player_id
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.striker
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.match_id) > 0
views.description: Per-player aggregates across all matches: total runs (sum of runs_scored where player was striker) and distinct matches played (count distinct match_id). Exposes raw measures needed to compute player-level average runs per match.

views.name: over_level_run_components
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bec.match_id,
  bec.innings_no,
  bec.over_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(bec.batsman_runs), 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(bec.extra_runs), 0) AS extra_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(bec.batsman_runs), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(bec.extra_runs), 0) AS total_runs
FROM
  ball_events_canonical AS bec
GROUP BY
  bec.match_id,
  bec.innings_no,
  bec.over_id
views.description: Per match / innings / over aggregated run components: total runs scored by batsmen and total extra runs (separately and combined). Keeps one row per match_id, innings_no, over_id with NULLs normalized to zeros.

views.name: over_any_ball_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.bowler AS bowler_id,
  b.team_bowling
FROM ball_by_ball b
GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id
views.description: Provides one representative bowler_id for each match/innings/over by selecting any ball_by_ball row for that over. Exposes match, innings, over and a single bowler_id (and optionally team_bowling).

views.name: match_innings_highest_over_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.match_id,
  o.innings_no,
  o.over_id,
  o.total_runs,
  b.bowler_id AS bowler_id,
  o.batsman_runs,
  o.extra_runs
FROM
  over_level_run_components o
LEFT JOIN
  over_any_ball_bowler b
ON
  o.match_id = b.match_id
  AND o.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND o.over_id = b.over_id
grain: one row per match_id, innings_no, over_id
views.description: Denormalized per-match-innings over-level rows combining total runs and a representative bowler. Useful to pick the highest-scoring over per match innings.

views.name: ball_event_with_match_and_players
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bep.match_id,
  bep.season_id,
  bep.over_id,
  bep.ball_id,
  bep.innings_no,
  bep.team_batting,
  bep.team_bowling,
  bep.striker,
  bep.non_striker,
  bep.bowler
FROM ball_event_with_players bep
views.description: One row per ball delivery enriched with match season and the participating player ids (striker, non_striker, bowler) and teams. Keeps raw identifiers to allow aggregation of runs or linking wickets to bowlers and seasons.

views.name: wicket_event_with_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  m.season_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out,
  b.bowler AS bowler_player_id
FROM wicket_taken w
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
JOIN "match" m
  ON w.match_id = m.match_id
grain: one_row_per_wicket_event (wicket_taken row joined to ball_by_ball and match)
views.description: Per-wicket events joined to the corresponding ball to attribute the wicket to the bowler and to the match season. Exposes dismissal kind, dismissed player, bowler id, and season so callers can filter dismissal kinds and aggregate wickets by bowler/season.

views.name: ball_events_with_players_and_innings_position
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bev.match_id,
  bev.innings_no,
  bev.over_id,
  bev.ball_id,
  bev.team_batting,
  bev.team_bowling,
  bev.striker,
  bev.non_striker,
  bev.bowler,
  COALESCE(brb.runs_scored, bbs.batsman_runs, dr.extra_runs, 0) AS runs_scored
FROM ball_event_with_players AS bev
LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball AS brb
  ON brb.match_id = bev.match_id
  AND brb.innings_no = bev.innings_no
  AND brb.over_id = bev.over_id
  AND brb.ball_id = bev.ball_id
LEFT JOIN ball_events_canonical AS bbs
  ON bbs.match_id = bev.match_id
  AND bbs.innings_no = bev.innings_no
  AND bbs.over_id = bev.over_id
  AND bbs.ball_id = bev.ball_id
LEFT JOIN delivery_runs_and_extras AS dr
  ON dr.match_id = bev.match_id
  AND dr.innings_no = bev.innings_no
  AND dr.over_id = bev.over_id
  AND dr.ball_id = bev.ball_id
views.description: One row per legal delivery/ball event with match, innings, over, ball identifiers, batting/bowling teams, striker/non-striker/bowler ids and the runs scored on that delivery (raw), suitable for reconstructing batting sequences and partnerships.

views.name: extras_per_ball
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.match_id,
  e.innings_no,
  e.over_id,
  e.ball_id,
  e.extra_type,
  e.extra_runs,
  CASE
    WHEN e.extra_type IN ('bye', 'legbyes') THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS extra_to_batsman_flag
FROM extra_runs e
views.description: One row per delivery listing extras on that delivery and a flag whether that extra type is credited to the batsman. Useful to compute partnership totals vs individual credited runs.

views.name: wicket_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out
FROM wickets_with_kind_and_player w
WHERE w.player_out IS NOT NULL
views.description: Rows representing wicket events in a match innings with the ball identifiers and the player dismissed. Useful to mark partnership boundaries (partnership starts after a wicket or at innings start and ends at next wicket/end of innings).

views.name: balls_with_extras_and_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS batsman_runs,
  er.extra_type,
  er.extra_runs,
  CASE
    WHEN er.extra_type IN ('wides','noballs') THEN 1
    WHEN er.extra_type IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_illegal_extra
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
views.description: Every delivery (ball) from ball_by_ball joined to any extra_runs and batsman_scored rows for the same delivery, canonicalizing presence of illegal extra types (wides/no-balls). Keeps one row per ball/innings with indicators and raw run values.

views.name: qualifying_wickets_attributed_to_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.innings_no,
  b.bowler AS bowler,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out
FROM
  wickets_with_kind_and_player w
JOIN
  ball_event_with_players b
ON
  w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
WHERE
  w.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'retired hurt', 'obstructing the field')
views.description: Wickets from wicket_taken joined to ball_by_ball to attribute the wicket to the bowler for the same delivery; excludes dismissal kinds that are not credited to the bowler (e.g., 'run out', 'retired hurt', 'obstructing the field'). Keeps one row per wicket event with attribution.

views.name: bowler_delivery_aggregates_per_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bev.match_id AS match_id,
  bev.bowler AS bowler_id,
  ms.match_date AS match_date,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_in_match,
  SUM(CASE WHEN bsr.runs_scored IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE bsr.runs_scored END) AS runs_conceded_in_match,
  COALESCE(w.wickets_in_match, 0) AS wickets_in_match
FROM
  ball_event_with_players AS bev
  JOIN match_summary_basic AS ms ON bev.match_id = ms.match_id
  LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball AS bsr
    ON bev.match_id = bsr.match_id
    AND bev.innings_no = bsr.innings_no
    AND bev.over_id = bsr.over_id
    AND bev.ball_id = bsr.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      bowler_player_id AS bowler,
      match_id,
      COUNT(*) AS wickets_in_match
    FROM wicket_event_with_bowler
    WHERE bowler_player_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY bowler_player_id, match_id
  ) AS w
    ON bev.bowler = w.bowler
    AND bev.match_id = w.match_id
WHERE
  bev.bowler IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  bev.bowler,
  bev.match_id,
  ms.match_date,
  w.wickets_in_match
views.description: Per-bowler, per-match aggregated raw measures computed from legal deliveries: total legal balls, total runs conceded off the bat (excluding extras), and qualifying wickets in that match. Useful for computing overall totals and selecting best single-match figures.

views.name: player_match_participation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  pm.role,
  pm.team_id
FROM player_match_roster pm
grain: match_id, player_id  -- one row per player's appearance in a match
views.description: Each player's participation in a match with role and team; one row per player-match. Useful to count matches played and to determine most frequent role.

views.name: player_ball_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  bep.striker,
  bep.non_striker,
  bep.bowler,
  COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  CASE WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dismissal,
  w.player_out,
  e.extra_type AS extra_runs_type,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  CASE WHEN br.runs_scored IS NOT NULL AND br.runs_scored > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS batsman_runs_flag
FROM
  ball_event_with_players bep
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
    ON bep.match_id = br.match_id
    AND bep.innings_no = br.innings_no
    AND bep.over_id = br.over_id
    AND bep.ball_id = br.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  wickets_with_kind_and_player w
    ON bep.match_id = w.match_id
    AND bep.innings_no = w.innings_no
    AND bep.over_id = w.over_id
    AND bep.ball_id = w.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  extras_per_ball_with_type e
    ON bep.match_id = e.match_id
    AND bep.innings_no = e.innings_no
    AND bep.over_id = e.over_id
    AND bep.ball_id = e.ball_id
INNER JOIN
  (SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id FROM ball_event_with_players) b
    ON bep.match_id = b.match_id
    AND bep.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND bep.over_id = b.over_id
    AND bep.ball_id = b.ball_id
grain: match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id  -- one row per delivery event
views.description: Ball-level events attributed to players: batting deliveries (runs scored, striker, balls faced) and wicket events (dismissals and wicket taker) joined per match/innings/ball. Exposes raw counts so career aggregates (runs, balls faced, dismissals, wickets, runs conceded to bowlers) can be computed.
